CONTEXT DUMP — T276 model-label normalization (deepseek-v4-flash/T276, follow-up to the deliverable at findings/T276-model-labels.json and commit af41bf5).

## 1. What I read
- untracked/T276-model-label-normalization.md (the brief), AGENTS.md, docs/infra/delegation/DELEGATEE.md (identity table + fresh-console traps).
- docs/infra/model-perf.md in full (2986 lines) — every alias-bearing line plus surrounding context.
- tools/gen-indices in full; src/claims_register.zig (parseRegister, splitCells, stripPunct); src/claimlint.zig (C7 parseFindingsFile, edge census, calibration harness); src/managent/main.zig (cmdAgent, cmdSet, cmdDone attribution enforcement, claim); findings-schema.json; findings/T226-context.json and T271-axioms.json as shape references; the three docs/INDEX-claim-*.md files before and after regeneration; git commits c344f02 (Orcha's own normalization precedent) and 91f7cf3 (where my kanban sweep landed); directive D013 via bin/managent inbox T276.

## 2. What I concluded, and on what evidence
- The brief's 112-line count is grep -c -i -E 'dspro|dsflash' on model-perf.md — reproduced exactly.
- model-perf.md: the ledger can only answer 'how did this model do' if the aggregation surfaces AND the attribution rows use one spelling. I renamed all model spellings including the model part of worker identifiers (DSPro/2B-3-AUDIT -> deepseek-v4-pro/2B-3-AUDIT) — 135 lines, content otherwise byte-identical (verified by diff review). 8 residual lines remain, each with a documented reason (my own note, a vendor reference, a quoted rule name x2, a verbatim historical passage x2). Evidence: the post-sweep word-bounded scan and the full diff.
- tasks.json: swept 15 agent rows via bin/managent agent only (12 DSPro -> deepseek-v4-pro, 2 DSFlash -> deepseek-v4-flash, T276 none -> deepseek-v4-flash). Evidence: the binary's own output, plus a post-hoc json scan showing zero alias rows except T227's model field. The sweep is in git at 91f7cf3 — a concurrent agent's commit swept up the working-tree change; verified HEAD carries all 15 canonical rows.
- tools/gen-indices: three same-class lies (forged Model: DSPro x3, hardcoded 274 claims, hardcoded edge counts). The root defect behind the edge counts is that the generator split the depends-on cell on ';' but the register writes comma-separated backtick spans — it silently dropped every edge after the first per row and left a trailing comma on the first (GLOBAL.AXIOM-LH rendered parent 'd:GLOBAL.FP1,'). I fixed the parse to mirror src/claims_register.zig (escaped-pipe cell split + backtick spans). Evidence: after the fix the generator's census (147 d:, 173 e:, 19 n:) matches claimlint's authoritative census exactly; before it read 146/93/11.
- C7 unabsorbed climbed 4 -> 8 during my session; every new entry traces to concurrent agents' findings files (T267-key-agreement.json committed at 52cd9c5; T266-incompleteness.json, T272-gate-hook.json, T274-tie-experiment.json in flight), not to my work. Evidence: git status of findings/ and the C7 listing. My two findings files (empty claims arrays) add 0.
- managent audit: 73 warnings at baseline, 71 at close (concurrent task closings resolved warnings; no gain from my changes).

## 3. What I could not establish
- Whether the Orcha intended identifier renames in model-perf.md or wanted identifiers preserved as historical record. The brief's '112 alias lines' + 'zero is the target' reading supports renaming; the T120 section's own precedent (corrected tally keeps raw identifiers) supports the opposite. I chose the rename with the derivation written into the file note and the commit so an independent seat can adjudicate.
- How the original author computed the hardcoded '97 d:, 11 n:, 91 e:' — whether from the broken ';'-split parse or some other graph definition. I only established the true current census and that the e: figure understates the register ~2x (173 vs 91).
- Whether any document or reader was misled by the generator's dropped edges before this fix (the INDEX files were regenerated 2026-08-01 with the broken parse; I did not audit their historical readers).
- Whether T227's model field (still 'DSPro') can ever be corrected: bin/managent has no writer for the model field — only agent — so the residue stands unless the binary grows a feature or the field is deprecated.
- The vendor-vs-model reading of 'spend DeepSeek vs Ollama-model budget': I treated DeepSeek as the API service (vendor), but it could be read as the model family. Left as-is either way.

## 4. What I assumed without checking
- That renaming identifiers in model-perf does not need cross-file consistency with other documents that cite those identifiers (PROGRESS.md, dispatch briefs) — the brief scopes this task to model-perf.md; I did not grep the repo for the old identifier spellings.
- That the managent binary's read-modify-write of tasks.json is safe against concurrent writers within the microsecond window — I verified outcome integrity (no lost claims) rather than the locking discipline; the binary rebuild banner showed dirty builds throughout (src changes without bin/ redeploy).
- That 'record none' (Task/Role/Model n/a) is the right honest generator stamp — I did not seriously explore detecting the real runner from the environment; the brief explicitly allows recording none.
- That the two 'not DeepSeek for Zig' occurrences are quotes of one historical rule and that leaving them quoted is safe; I did not locate the rule's original wording.
- That the deps index's 'see kanban' status column and its 'Status is from the kanban' prose are acceptable placeholders, not number-lies requiring action.

## 5. What I noticed but did not act on
- The task index prose 'Status is from the kanban' with every row showing the static string 'see kanban' — a soft placeholder, not an asserted count; left (borderline, flagged here).
- claimlint's output renders oddly when redirected to a file (embedded carriage returns; a redirected capture held only the tail's visual fragments). I worked around it with tr '\r' '\n' rather than reporting it.
- GLOBAL.TIE-MIGOS's depends-on cell contains prose inside the backtick span area ('(the measurement, whose prior explanation this row corrects)') — both claimlint and the fixed generator ignore non-prefixed spans, so behavior matches, but prose in the edge column is fragile and could silently drop edges if it ever starts with d:/e:/n:.
- findings/T271-axioms.json uses key 'task' instead of the schema's 'task_id' and omits 'claims' — non-conforming per findings-schema.json; claimlint's C7 silently treats its task_id as empty. Noted; T271's file predates my task and was not in my scope.
- The pre-existing audit warning that zig-out/bin/managent is newer than bin/managent (deploy it) — a concurrent-session artifact I did not fix.
- Repeated-narrowing smells (A: 5), C1a=10 orphans, C2=14 dangling paths, C3=78 debt — all pre-existing and out of scope; I verified only that my changes did not move them.
